speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Stuff is in the code, every new feature that gets developed is off of the same code.
zh: 东西都在代码里，每个开发出来的新功能都在同一个代码上。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: And our product manager can go and review it and they can polish it using our platform and get the UI and UX exactly right and see all the bad decisions from the user-facing perspective that the developer made.
zh: 我们的产品经理可以去审查它，他们可以使用我们的平台来打磨它，并让 UI 和 UX 完全正确，看看开发者从用户视角做出的所有糟糕决策。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Well, the developer got the feature working, it did not get the feature polished.
zh: 嗯，开发者让功能运作起来了，并没有把功能打磨好。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: So that's fine.
zh: 所以这没问题。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: We have other personas for it.
zh: 我们还有其他角色来做这个。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: And now they can do their work in a way that is smooth within the evolving code base, like it's evolving really quickly.
zh: 现在他们可以在一个正在演进的代码库中以顺畅的方式完成他们的工作，就像它演进得非常快。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Uh so that kind of feature flagging, merging quickly with feature flags enables us to do it kind of two-step.
zh: 嗯所以那种功能开关，带功能开关快速合并使我们能够做这种两步法。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: There's no one PR.
zh: 没有单一的拉取请求。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: A feature should take three or four PRs, one PR from the developer, one PR from the product manager that changes functionality, one PR from the designer that tunes the UIUEX, and then maybe one last PR from the QA that saw some sort of itch case.
zh: 一个功能应该花三到四个拉取请求，一个来自开发者的拉取请求，一个来自改变功能的产品经理的拉取请求，一个来自调整 UIUEX 的设计师的拉取请求，然后也许还有来自 QA 的最后一个拉取请求，他看到了某种痒痒案例。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And in terms of like the the human reviewer being the slowdown there, I had a really interesting chat with uh Ryan Lapopoli, who's a member of technical staff at uh OpenAI.
zh: 就人工审查员在那儿成为拖累而言，我和 uh Ryan Lapopoli 进行了一次非常有趣的聊天，他是 uh OpenAI 的一名技术人员。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And um one of the things that they're doing in some of their projects is to entirely remove uh a human reviewer.
zh: 嗯他们在一些项目中所做的一件事是完全移除 uh 人工审查员。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Uh, how much does that make you go, oh gosh, that's horrible?

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Or how much does that make you think, oh wow, there's a real opportunity here in certain cases for us to actually allow either an AI or tooling to perform those uh reviews and give us that feedback, maybe for different levels of criticality of change.
zh: 或者这让你有多少觉得，哦哇，在某些情况下这里有一个真正的机会让我们实际上允许 AI 或工具来执行那些 uh 审查并给我们那个反馈，也许是针对不同级别的变更关键性。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: But is that something that you look at, Mike, much?
zh: 但这是你经常关注的事情吗，Mike？

en: Oh, all the time.
zh: 哦，一直都在。

en: Yeah.

en: So again, it goes back to the risk uh conversation.

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: High risk, no way.
zh: 高风险，没门。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Uh I want a human person.
zh: 嗯我想要一个人。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: And I also define like risk is also by what part of the code base they're touching, how sensitive it is.
zh: 而且我也定义像风险也是由他们接触代码库的哪一部分，它有多敏感来决定的。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Uh but beyond it, I'm trying to automate the PR commenting and comment resolution process, uh, which means I have uh agents that have modeled every single developer on my team and their comments for the last few hundred PRs.
zh: 嗯但除此之外，我正在尝试自动化拉取请求评论和评论解决过程，uh，这意味着我有 uh 智能体，它们为我团队上的每一个开发者建模，以及他们在过去几百个拉取请求中的评论。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: And I know each and every persona.
zh: 而且我知道每一个角色。

en: So as soon as a PR is open, we have a whole prepare PR, which is a bunch of agents to check it in all the ways that we've modeled it, we need to check it.

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Once a PR is open, we launch different agents that model different people from our team and comment as if they were those people, and does a surprisingly good job.

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Then we trigger agents again to resolve those comments.
zh: 然后我们再次触发智能体来解决这些评论。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Then we trigger the retro to see are there any error logs, stuff actually behaves like it wanted to.
zh: 然后我们触发 retro 来看看是否有任何错误日志，东西实际上表现得像它想要的那样。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: And again, if the risk is not high from the PR's nature, I'm moving towards being able to like skip the human reviewer at all.

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: Uh but I'm definitely pushing for that.
zh: 嗯，但我肯定在推动这件事。

speaker: Tamuz Dubnov
en: And it depends how reversible it is as well, in terms of uh It's the cardrails, right?

speaker: Daniel Jones

zh: 所以嗯 Adevo 的一个客户，嗯他们正在做一些非常伟大的工作，他们有一个团队已经完全智能体化，他们改变了他们的开发流程嗯嗯嗯去嗯在许多不同方面拥抱 AI，需求收集，转录，故事编写，实现，所有这类事情，他们现在快了 72 倍。

en: So they've uh done great things there.

en: Before they self-merge their PR, uh they run about seven or eight uh code reviews, different tools looking at different things, and their confidence is uh they've been doing that, that they're now confident enough that they don't need uh humans to look at it.

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: And I think there's something interesting, I don't know how true this is.
zh: 我认为有一些有趣的事情，我不知道这有多真实。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Um I mean, data is definitely like when you screw up data, your data is gone.
zh: 嗯我的意思是，数据肯定是就像当你搞砸数据时，你的数据就没了。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Do we need to move to event sourcing and having a you know a replayable history of all data transformations?
zh: 我们需要转移到事件溯源并拥有一个你知道所有数据转换的可重放历史吗？

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: That's one thing.
zh: 那是一件事。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: But like generally, as a trend, we've always seen that trying to prevent bad things happen by putting a check in place is the wrong answer.
zh: 但通常来说，作为一种趋势，我们总是看到试图通过设置

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Like with data and databases, we went from like having transactions to prevent inconsistencies happening.
zh: 就像数据和数据库一样，我们从拥有事务来防止不一致性发生开始。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: That was slow, it doesn't scale.
zh: 那很慢，它无法扩展。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: So, what was the answer?
zh: 那么，答案是什么？

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Eventual consistency, and we'll reconcile.
zh: 最终一致性，并且我们会去协调。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: After the fact.
zh: 事后。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: With the cloud native transformation, we found out that you know you can't have a thousand microservices and then integration test them all.
zh: 随着云原生转型，我们发现你知道你不能拥有一千个微服务然后对它们全部进行集成测试。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: You just have to deploy them and find out what happens.
zh: 你只需要部署它们并看看会发生什么。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: So you need great observability and you need to be able to fix forward very quickly.
zh: 所以你需要极佳的可观测性，并且你需要能够非常快速地向前修复。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: So again, you let the bad thing happen, but you react to it more quickly.
zh: 所以同样，你让坏事情发生，但你对此反应得更快。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: I imagine that where we might end up with uh agentic coding is something like outcome-driven development where you've got observability of the business impact you wanted a feature to have.
zh: 我想我们最终在 uh 智能体编码方面可能会达到的境地是类似结果驱动开发，在其中你拥有你希望某个功能具备的业务影响力的可观测性。

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Like, is the application doing the things the application is supposed to do?
zh: 比如，应用程序是否在执行应用程序应该做的事情？

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Are users able to do what they should be able to do?
zh: 用户是否能够做他们应该能够做的事情？

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: And then we have software factories chucking features out, and then you look for regressions in like, okay, the number of checkouts uh on the shopping cart has has um uh has dropped and reacting and fixing forward at that point.

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Is that something you feel users are gonna accept?

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Just as we've got used to waking up and finding out that you know the Apple have decided to change like how the photo album works, and our elderly parents are now very annoyed.

speaker: Daniel Jones
en: Um, do we end up with something like that on a more daily basis, like this rapid churn of um features changing and being slightly different, but like I can still achieve the outcome?
